summary: Multiplexed signed-url retry loop counted as separate requests causing opaque 429s and console credit mismatch
description: Customer reports repeated 429s during large multipart import where our rate limiter shows bursts from a single API key. Console credit counters appear higher (less consumed) than runtime rate limiter, creating confusion about quota depletion. Issue started after the customer migrated their upload workers behind a retry-proxy that appends a tracing query param to callbacks.
impact: Multiple background ingestion pipelines at Streamline Analytics are failing to complete nightly backfills. Visible symptom: steady stream of 429s for upload-callback POSTs originating from the customer's worker fleet; end-users see backfill job failures and missed SLAs.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Configure a dedicated tenant with multipart storage callbacks enabled.
2) Deploy an upload worker behind a proxy that performs retries and appends a unique query parameter (?trace_id=...) on replay.
3) Start parallel multipart uploads that trigger signed-url-callbacks to Redwood callback endpoint.
4) Force intermittent failures on the callback path so the proxy retries, replaying the callback with unique query strings.
5) Observe increased 429s on the tenant and a mismatch between Console 'remaining credits' and runtime rate-limit denied requests.
logs:
2026-03-10T02:13:40Z gateway rate-limiter DENY tenant=streamline key=sk_live_XXX path=/v1/uploads/callback status=429 reason=token-exhausted
2026-03-10T02:13:41Z gateway rate-limiter DENY tenant=streamline key=sk_live_XXX path=/v1/uploads/callback?trace_id=abc123 status=429 reason=token-exhausted
2026-03-10T02:13:42Z billing aggregator ingest credit-usage tenant=streamline delta=+1200 tokens (deduped)
Console shows remaining_credits: 12,345 while rate-limiter logs indicate sustained denials. Cobrowsing screenshot uploaded to ticket.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: gateway token-bucket is keyed on full request URI (including query string) causing retries with new query params to be treated as distinct windows and double-counting. Billing aggregation pipeline deduplicates callbacks by callback-id in body, hence console shows fewer unique consumptions. Verified via sampling: 1 physical upload produced 3 distinct rate-limiter entries (different query strings) but a single billing record. Confirmed request header differences: proxy adds X-Retry-Index and appends ?trace_id on retry. Related metrics: rate_limit.window_usage spiked to 300% of expected during proxy retry waves. Cross-referenced with dedicated-pool autoscaler metrics: no GPU saturation; this is allocation of request tokens at ingress.
comments: Support (Asha): Customer provided a replayable curl example and pcap. Asked to confirm whether gateway normalizes query params for rate accounting.

SRE (Liam): Reproduced locally with a small proxy that appends ?r=UUID; observed identical behavior. Created a minimal test that shows rate-limiter keying by full request path. Adding as linked issue for gateway change.

Support (Asha): Noted console and billing team treat callbacks as idempotent using callback_id in the body, which explains the visible credit mismatch. Customer is worried about opaque 429s and lack of correlation in Console.

Eng (Riley Chen): Proposed short-term mitigation: recommend disabling query-param append on proxy retries or add 'X-Original-Callback-Id' header from uploader so gateway can dedupe for rate accounting. Filed gateway PR to normalize callback path for rate-limiter (see related PR).
Customer (S. Rivera): Confirmed they can change proxy behavior but prefer a platform-side fix for long-run since multiple clients use proxy.
Billing (Marta): Confirmed billing accuracy is preserved; aggregation dedupes by callback_id. Console display will be extended in follow-up to call out dedupe timeframe.
root_cause: Gateway rate-limiter keyed on full request URI including transient query params introduced by retry proxies; billing pipeline deduplicates by callback_id leading to apparent mismatch between Console credits and rate-limiter denials.
resolution: Short-term workaround: customer disabled query-param splaying on retry-proxy and enabled X-Original-Callback-Id header; retries now preserve callback_id in header and 429s stopped. Long-term fix: gateway change to normalize signed-url callback paths for rate accounting (strip known tracing query params and prefer callback-id header if present). Patch merged: github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/1492. Console note: added a tooltip explaining deduplication logic for callbacks and billing display.
resolution_notes: Patch rolled out to dedicated-pool edge in us-east-1 on 2026-03-12 with canary at 5% then 100% after 30m. Post-deploy monitoring: rate-limiter DENY events for tenant dropped by 98% during a replay test. Customer confirmed nightly backfills completed on 2026-03-12 run.
follow_up_actions:
1) Add docs entry in runbook for 'signed-url callback best practices' and recommended headers.
2) Console: surface dedupe vs raw runtime discrepancy in billing pane.
3) Add e2e test that simulates retry-proxy query param splay to prevent regressions.
4) Consider making query-param normalization configurable per-tenant for private deployments.
